repos.title: ChatGLM: A Family of Large Language Models from GLM-130B to GLM-4 All Tools
repos.paper_summary: This report introduces the GLM-4 family of large language models, including GLM-4, GLM-4-Air, and the open-source GLM-4-9B. The models are pre-trained on 10 trillion tokens of mostly Chinese and English text and aligned via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback. On academic benchmarks, GLM-4 (0520) scores 83.3 on MMLU and 78.5 on HumanEval, approaching GPT-4 (0613) scores of 86.4 and 67.0, respectively. For long-context tasks, GLM-4 achieves 87.3 on LongBench-Chat English, matching GPT-4 Turbo (1106) at 87.2. In Chinese alignment, GLM-4 outperforms GPT-4 and matches GPT-4 Turbo on AlignBench. The GLM-4 All Tools variant autonomously selects external tools like web browsers and Python interpreters; it matches or exceeds GPT-4 All Tools on information seeking and math solving. Limitations include lower performance than GPT-4 Turbo on mathematics and agent tasks involving operating systems or knowledge graphs.

repos.title: Nerfstudio: A Modular Framework for Neural Radiance Field Development
repos.paper_summary: Nerfstudio is a modular PyTorch framework for Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) development that consolidates reusable components for data processing, model training, real-time visualization, and geometry export. It includes Nerfacto, a default method combining techniques from MipNeRF-360, Instant-NGP, NeRF-W, and Ref-NeRF. The framework organizes the pipeline into DataManagers, Models, Fields, and Losses, allowing users to swap components without rewriting code. A web-based viewer uses WebRTC to stream rendered frames during training, enabling interactive qualitative assessment of unseen views. On the MipNeRF-360 dataset, Nerfacto achieves 28.0 dB PSNR after 70K iterations (~30 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX A5000), compared to 29.2 dB for MipNeRF-360 which requires several hours on a TPU. Ablations on a new 10-scene in-the-wild dataset show that removing scene contraction drops PSNR from 21.0 dB to 18.6 dB. The paper notes that standard metrics like PSNR can be misleading for real-world captures where evaluation images are close to training poses, highlighting the need for visual inspection.

repos.title: UFO: A UI-Focused Agent for Windows OS Interaction
repos.paper_summary:
UFO is a UI-focused agent for Windows that uses GPT-Vision to execute natural language requests across desktop applications. The system employs a dual-agent framework: a HostAgent selects the target application and creates a global plan, while an AppAgent iteratively executes specific actions on UI controls. A Control Interaction module grounds these decisions using `pywinauto` and the Windows UI Automation API to perform operations like clicking buttons or setting text. UFO supports cross-application tasks by switching contexts and storing execution results in shared memory.

The authors evaluate UFO on WindowsBench, a custom benchmark of 50 tasks spanning nine applications including Outlook, Word, and Edge. UFO achieves an 86% success rate and 89.6% completion rate, outperforming GPT-4 (42% success) and GPT-3.5 (24% success) baselines, which rely on human surrogates for action execution. UFO also completes tasks in fewer steps (5.48 average) than the baselines. Limitations include restricted support for applications not fully compatible with Windows UI Automation, such as Adobe Acrobat, and potential delays when navigating unfamiliar interfaces.

repos.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
repos.paper_summary:
This paper presents a method for high-quality image synthesis using diffusion probabilistic models. The authors demonstrate that training on a weighted variational bound, derived from an equivalence to denoising score matching, yields superior sample quality compared to standard likelihood-based objectives.

The model learns to reverse a Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to data. By parameterizing the reverse process mean as a function that predicts the added noise $\epsilon$, the training objective simplifies to minimizing the expected squared error between true and predicted noise:

$$
L_{\mathrm{simple}}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{t, \mathbf{x}_0, \epsilon} \left[ \| \epsilon - \epsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t}\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar{\alpha}_t}\epsilon, t) \|^2 \right]
$$

where $t$ is the time step, $\mathbf{x}_0$ is the data, and $\epsilon$ is standard Gaussian noise. Sampling proceeds by iteratively removing noise using this learned predictor. On unconditional CIFAR10, the model achieves an Inception score of 9.46 and a FID score of 3.17, outperforming previous unconditional baselines like SNGAN-DDLS (FID 15.4). On 256x256 LSUN datasets, it produces samples with FID scores of 7.89 for churches and 4.90 for bedrooms. A limitation noted in the analysis is that while sample quality is high, the lossless codelengths are not competitive with other likelihood-based models, as most bits describe imperceptible details.

repos.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
repos.paper_summary:
Grad-CAM produces coarse localization heatmaps for any Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) without architectural changes or re-training. It computes neuron importance weights $\alpha_k^c$ by globally averaging the gradients of a target class score $y^c$ with respect to the final convolutional layer activations $A^k$. The heatmap is generated via a ReLU-applied linear combination of these forward activation maps.

The paper proves Grad-CAM generalizes Class Activation Mapping (CAM) by showing that CAM’s fixed weights are proportional to Grad-CAM’s gradient-derived weights when global average pooling precedes the softmax. On the ILSVRC-15 validation set, Grad-CAM applied to VGG-16 achieves a top-1 localization error of 56.5%, outperforming c-MWP (70.9%) and Backprop (61.1%). For weakly-supervised segmentation on PASCAL VOC 2012, using Grad-CAM as seeds yields an Intersection over Union of 49.6, compared to 44.6 for CAM. Human studies indicate Guided Grad-CAM improves class discrimination accuracy from 44.4% to 61.2%. A limitation is that the method relies on the assumption that final convolutional layers capture both semantic meaning and spatial detail; visualizations degrade when applied to earlier layers with smaller receptive fields.

repos.title: EchoMimic: Lifelike Audio-Driven Portrait Animations through Editable Landmark Conditions
repos.paper_summary:
EchoMimic is a diffusion-based model for generating talking head videos from a single reference image, driven by audio, facial landmarks, or a combination of both. The architecture extends Stable Diffusion with three specialized modules: a Reference U-Net to preserve identity, an Audio Encoder using Wav2Vec features, and a Landmark Encoder that adds spatial constraints via element-wise addition to the latent space. A two-stage training strategy first learns static image-to-motion mappings, then trains temporal attention layers on 12-frame video sequences. To enable mixed driving modes, the authors use Random Landmark Selection during training, randomly dropping facial parts like eyes or mouth to force the model to rely on other signals.

On the HDTF dataset, EchoMimic achieves a FID of 29.136 and FVD of 492.784, outperforming baselines including SadTalker (FID 41.535) and Hallo (FID 37.659). On CelebV-HQ, it records the lowest FID of 63.258 among compared methods. An ablation study shows that landmark-only driving yields higher structural similarity (SSIM 0.889) than audio-only driving (SSIM 0.812), while the combined mode offers intermediate control. Limitations include the reliance on an image-based diffusion backbone rather than a native video transformer, and the absence of acceleration techniques for real-time inference.

repos.title: Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models
repos.paper_summary: Chameleon is a family of early-fusion, token-based mixed-modal models that generate and understand arbitrary sequences of interleaved images and text. The architecture quantizes 512x512 images into 1024 discrete tokens from an 8192 codebook, allowing a single transformer to process both modalities without separate encoders. To stabilize training, which diverged in standard Llama architectures due to norm growth, the authors implement query-key normalization, z-loss regularization, and reordered layer norms. Chameleon-34B was trained on 9.2 trillion tokens using 3,072 GPUs. On human evaluations of long-form mixed-modal generation, Chameleon-34B achieved a 60.4% preference rate over Gemini Pro and 51.6% over GPT-4V. It outperforms Flamingo and IDEFICS on image captioning benchmarks while matching Mixtral 8x7B on text-only tasks like MMLU (65.8 vs 70.6). Limitations include weak performance on OCR-heavy tasks due to tokenizer constraints and exclusion of chart interpretation from their primary human evaluation set.

repos.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
repos.paper_summary: HippoRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses a knowledge graph and Personalized PageRank to enable multi-hop reasoning in a single retrieval step. It builds an offline index by extracting open information extraction triples from passages using an LLM, forming a schemaless knowledge graph. During online retrieval, the system identifies query entities, maps them to graph nodes, and runs Personalized PageRank with these nodes as seeds to propagate probability mass across associated concepts. Passage scores are calculated by aggregating node probabilities over the documents containing them. On MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA benchmarks, HippoRAG achieves recall@5 scores of 51.9% and 89.1%, respectively, outperforming baselines like ColBERTv2 and RAPTOR. Compared to iterative methods like IRCoT, it is 10–30 times cheaper and 6–13 times faster while maintaining comparable accuracy. Limitations include reliance on off-the-shelf components without fine-tuning, which leads to errors in entity extraction and OpenIE, and unverified scalability beyond current benchmark sizes.

repos.title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
repos.paper_summary:
ColPali is a document retrieval model that generates multi-vector embeddings directly from document page images using a Vision Language Model, eliminating the need for text extraction pipelines. The paper also introduces ViDoRe, a benchmark of 10 tasks covering diverse domains and languages to evaluate visually rich document retrieval.

The method extends PaliGemma-3B by adding a projection layer to map output embeddings to a 128-dimensional space. It uses a late interaction mechanism where the score between a query $q$ and document $d$ is computed as:

$$
\text{LI}(q,d) = \sum_{i=1}^{N_q} \max_{j=1}^{N_d} \langle \mathbf{E}_q^{(i)} | \mathbf{E}_d^{(j)} \rangle
$$

where $\mathbf{E}_q$ and $\mathbf{E}_d$ are the multi-vector representations. The model is trained with LoRA adapters on 127,460 query-page pairs. On ViDoRe, ColPali achieves an average NDCG@5 of 81.3, outperforming the best baseline (Unstructured + Captioning with BGE-M3) at 67.0. Indexing latency is significantly lower than parsing-based methods because it skips OCR and layout detection steps. Limitations include a high memory footprint of 256 KB per page and reliance on vector databases with native multi-vector support.

repos.title: SadTalker: Learning Realistic 3D Motion Coefficients for Stylized Audio-Driven Single Image Talking Face Animation
repos.paper_summary: SadTalker generates audio-driven talking head videos from a single image by predicting 3DMM motion coefficients. The method decouples expression and head pose generation to reduce uncertainty in the coupled 2D motion fields. ExpNet learns facial expression coefficients by distilling lip-only targets from Wav2Lip and applying perceptual losses on rendered 3D faces, while PoseVAE uses a conditional VAE to synthesize diverse head poses based on audio and style identity. A separate face render maps these coefficients to unsupervised 3D keypoints to warp the source image. On the HDTF dataset, SadTalker achieves an FID of 22.057, CPBD of 0.335, and CSIM of 0.843, outperforming baselines like Audio2Head (FID 24.392) and MakeItTalk (FID 28.243). User studies indicate 54.8% preference for overall quality compared to 14.7% for Audio2Head. Limitations include artifacts in teeth synthesis due to 3DMM constraints and a fixed emotional expression that does not vary with the audio content.
